- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential mean reversion or rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the 10–15 day horizon after recent spikes; apply downward correction for short-term momentum.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-stage price corrections; add a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from 1.00 to 0.33), model lags in adjusting; apply early correction to avoid lagged overreaction.
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs; cap forecast at 10–15% below the immediate prior peak if sentiment is cooling.
